note: The cut of the animated film 'Wish You Were Here' (75 s, 24 frames a second). Shots are rendered by the Unity film renderer (native/quest/Assets/SameSky/Editor/Film/FilmWish*.cs) to demo-build/wish/shots/<id>.mp4 and put in this order. The film runs on a grid of 96 beats a minute: a beat is 0.625 s (15 frames), a bar 2.5 s, and every cut is on a beat. 'at' times are seconds from the start of the film. scripts/demo/wish_audio.py makes the sound and wish_edit.py the picture from this file.

shots.what: An aerial over Adam's harbour city at night: lit rooms with people in them, the quay, a boat crossing
Maya at the sea wall in the last sun, to the empty place beside her: 'You're missing the good part.'
Adam on his balcony in the blue hour: 'Maybe not tonight.' He pushes off the rail
Maya turns from the wall and sets off along the coast walk
Adam steps out of his street door, looks down a road of red tail lights, and walks
Adam through the lit back street, people all round him
Maya passes three musicians on the walk and lifts a hand to them
A stranger on a bench moves over and pats the place beside him
Adam's hand along the quay rail
Maya's hand along the sea wall (a match cut)
Cloths on a stall in the wind; her shadow crosses them with her
His feet on the wet paving, faster now
A straw hat gets away from its owner; Maya leans out of its way and laughs
Adam climbs the city stairway toward the light at its top
Maya climbs the steps above the coast (the same framing)
His profile, climbing, against the dark wall
Her profile, the same move, against the amber sea
Up the stairs behind him into the gate's light
Out of the light: an amber horizon, warm stone, a chair turned to the water
Climbing plants in the sun
Linen in the breeze
Maya at the terrace wall hears footsteps, and turns
The wide: from behind him on the last steps, up over the wall as they cross the terrace to each other; her sunset and his city's night in one sky
The embrace: her face, then his
Their hands meet
She pulls him by the hand toward the view
At the wall: he looks at her instead of the view, and she catches him
He brings the second chair over beside hers
Both laughing
The two of them, small, under the one sky
'Took you long enough.' 'Traffic.' It lands; they turn to the horizon
Up over their heads into the sky: SAMESKY, then 'Far apart. Right here.'
'Same time tomorrow?' He pulls his chair closer. Cut to black
